source.title: Scaling Distributed Training with Adaptive Summation
source.authors: Saeed Maleki; M. Musuvathi; T. Mytkowicz; Olli Saarikivi; Tian-Ju Xu; Vadim Eksarevskiy; Jaliya Ekanayake; E. Barsoum

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Compares large-batch training with an adaptive gradient-combination method and reports held-out accuracy or convergence outcomes, a different method for testing the large-batch penalty.
record.gate_note: Tests V5 through its own comparisons of synchronous gradient summation and Adasum at different effective batch sizes. The paper does not test the other claim versions. Cited optimizer and large-batch results are not extracted as study results.
record.test_reason: The ImageNet synchronous-SGD comparison and the fixed-two-epoch MNIST experiments test V5. Several other rows report Adasum's performance without a controlled comparison of held-out performance across batch sizes.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that Adasum enables ResNet-50 Momentum-SGD at 64K, BERT-Adam at 64K, and BERT-LAMB at 128K examples before communication while maintaining downstream targets, and improves convergence in some matched-batch comparisons. These conclusions do not establish equal-epoch accuracy preservation for every configuration.
record.recipe_differences: Replaces ordinary gradient summation with Adasum, which adaptively combines gradients to emulate sequential SGD; experiments compare optimizer and batch-size configurations rather than testing the original generalization-gap interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with gradient-combination method, effective batch size, learning-rate tuning, and GPU count.

fits_no_version.finding: TensorFlow ResNet-50 reaches the target in 68 epochs with communication every local step and 84 epochs with communication every 16 local updates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Less frequent communication with local SGD updates can reduce communication costs while increasing data needed to reach target accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Adasum-Adam and Adasum-LAMB achieve BERT downstream targets, and Adasum-LAMB reduces iterations relative to LAMB at matched batch sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive gradient combination can improve convergence or enable particular large-batch configurations without establishing equal-epoch generalization across batch sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Tuned Adasum outperforms tuned Sum at 16 GPUs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-combination methods differ in fixed-budget accuracy at a common batch size.

record.code_released: Horovod main branch; URL not stated
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Machine Learning and Systems
record.problems: Results focus on convergence and downstream accuracy rather than train-test error gaps. Several comparisons provide only qualitative accuracy statements or figure-based accuracy without exact values. Production-model results are summarized without detailed measurements.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying reported results were omitted.

untested.parts: Generalization across network widths beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning.

Controlled equal-epoch language-model batch-size comparisons; normalization and regularization interventions; systematic workload-dependent thresholds; final accuracy differences beyond the reported target-based comparisons.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.

missing.what: Separate the untuned Sum batch-scaling failure from R8's Adasum result: with two epochs fixed, sequential batch 32 reaches 99.3%, while Sum fails to converge above eight GPUs, corresponding to global batches 512 and 1024.

record.verdict_notes: Adasum's successful adapted configurations are consistent with V5's explicit adaptation qualification. No challenges verdict is warranted. Target-attainment comparisons establish threshold differences, not full final-accuracy curves or train–test generalization gaps.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error across widths beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance under different tuning regimes.

Language-model large-batch comparisons; fixed-epoch comparisons across workload-dependent batch thresholds; whether normalization or regularization changes close the penalty; same-epoch comparisons for all image classifiers.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measured properties tracking the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: PyTorch ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Synchronous SGD using Horovod Sum at effective batch size 16K
rows.value: Sum 16k never reaches 74.9% validation accuracy after 120 epochs
rows.note: The large-batch Sum run fails the stated target while the smaller-batch Sum run reaches it.
rows.check: The state is inverted: failure at 16K supports the large-batch penalty. Sum at 2K reaches 74.9% in 62 epochs; Sum at 16K remains below it after 120 epochs.

rows.subject: PyTorch ResNet-50
rows.note: Adasum reaches the target at 16K and takes fewer epochs than its 2K configuration.
rows.check: The epoch counts are swapped. Section 5.1.2 reports Adasum 2K: 62 epochs; Adasum 16K: 69 epochs. The adapted recipe retains a modest batch-size penalty rather than improving epochs to target.

rows.subject: TensorFlow ResNet-50 (MLPerf v0.5 reference implementation)
rows.operation_detail: Adasum-enabled distributed optimizer with local steps before communication
rows.baseline: Adasum with 16 local steps and effective batch size 4K: 68 epochs
rows.value: Adasum with 16 local steps and effective batch size 64K: 84 epochs
rows.note: Increasing effective batch size to 64K increases epochs to target, while the model still reaches the target.
rows.check: The 4K baseline uses one local step before communication, not 16. The 64K condition uses 16 local SGD updates before communication. This changes communication frequency while retaining local weight updates; it is not a comparison of ordinary 4K and 64K minibatches. The 68-versus-84-epoch result measures communication-interval scaling.

rows.subject: TensorFlow ResNet-50 (MLPerf v0.5 reference implementation)
rows.measure: Whether the run reaches 74.9% test accuracy
rows.value: Sum 16k plateaus below the target accuracy
rows.note: The text describes the Sum 16k run as plateauing below target; it does not provide a numeric final accuracy.
rows.check: Remove this duplicate and misattributed row. The Sum 16K plateau belongs to the PyTorch experiment in Section 5.1 and Figure 5, already recorded in R1. It is not a TensorFlow Sum 64K result.

rows.subject: BERT-Large
rows.operation_detail: Adasum-Adam at effective batch size 64K in Phase 1
rows.measure: Iterations to achieve target SQuAD score of 90.5
rows.uncertainty: Target score averaged over 5 tries with different seeds
rows.note: The study reports that Adasum-Adam converges at 64K using the same iteration counts as the LAMB baseline; this is not a comparison with smaller-batch Adam in this study.
rows.check: This compares optimizer recipes at the same batch sizes. It supplies no smaller-batch Adam control under an equal epoch budget. Adam's failure beyond 16K is attributed to prior work.

rows.subject: BERT-Large
rows.operation_detail: Adasum-LAMB at effective batch size 64K in Phase 1
rows.measure: Iterations to achieve target SQuAD score of 90.5
rows.uncertainty: Target score averaged over 5 tries with different seeds
rows.note: The study characterizes this as close to 20% faster convergence.
rows.check: This is Adasum's convergence improvement over LAMB at the same batch sizes, not a test of the batch-size penalty.

rows.subject: BERT-Large
rows.operation_detail: Adasum-LAMB at effective batch size 128K in Phase 1
rows.measure: Iterations to achieve target SQuAD score of 90.5
rows.uncertainty: Target score averaged over 5 tries with different seeds
rows.note: The paper reports reaching the target at 128K effective batch size.
rows.check: Reaching the target at 128K does not establish equal-budget accuracy preservation. Phase 1 processes 4574 × 128K examples, versus 7039 × 64K for baseline LAMB, approximately 30% more examples.

rows.subject: LeNet-5
rows.operation_detail: Adasum with momentum SGD, fixed two-epoch budget and untuned learning rate
rows.measure: Accuracy under aggressive sequential learning-rate schedule
rows.baseline: Sum fails to converge at more than 8 GPUs without learning-rate tuning
rows.value: Adasum converges at 32 GPUs without hyperparameter search
rows.note: The text gives no numeric accuracy for these configurations.
rows.check: For the large-batch penalty, successful Adasum convergence is an absent penalty, not an observed penalty. Specify batch size 32 per GPU, hence global batch 1024 at 32 GPUs, and the sequential 99.3% target under the same two-epoch budget. The untuned Sum failures above eight GPUs should be separated into a comparator row.

rows.subject: LeNet-5
rows.operation_detail: Adasum with momentum SGD, fixed two-epoch budget and tuned learning rate

conditions.value: tuned separately for method and GPU count

rows.measure: Accuracy under aggressive sequential learning-rate schedule
rows.value: Adasum 16 GPUs tuned learning rate 0.012; text says it beats Sum at 16 GPUs
rows.locator: Section 5.4, Figure 6 and tuned learning-rate table
rows.note: No numeric accuracy is stated for the comparison.
rows.check: The recorded result only compares Adasum with Sum at the same GPU count and batch size. Learning-rate values and an advantage over Sum do not establish accuracy preservation relative to smaller-batch training.

rows.subject: LeNet-5
rows.operation_detail: Sum with momentum SGD, fixed two-epoch budget and tuned learning rate
rows.measure: Accuracy under aggressive sequential learning-rate schedule
rows.value: Text says tuned Sum remains far below untuned Adasum at 32 GPUs
rows.locator: Section 5.4, Figure 6 and tuned learning-rate table
rows.note: Qualitative comparison; numeric accuracies are not stated.
rows.check: Use sequential training reaching 99.3% in two epochs as the reference, and specify global batch 1024 at 32 GPUs. The text reports tuned Sum substantially below untuned Adasum, which still converges under this budget. This supports a residual penalty; exact accuracy is unavailable in the supplied figure text.

relationships.condition: ImageNet ResNet-50 with ordinary synchronous Sum, 2K versus 16K batches
relationships.reason: R1: the 2K run reaches 74.9% in 62 epochs, whereas 16K remains below that target after 120 epochs.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports that, despite longer training, the larger batch did not reach the accuracy goal set for the smaller-batch run. This comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: ImageNet ResNet-50 with Adasum, 2K versus 16K batches
relationships.reason: R2, corrected: the adapted recipe reaches the target at both sizes, but increasing batch size raises epochs to target from 62 to 69, retaining a smaller penalty.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports that both batches reached the accuracy target with Adasum, which adaptively combines gradients across workers. Larger batches required more epochs, and this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: MNIST LeNet-5 with Adasum and the unchanged sequential learning-rate schedule, two epochs
relationships.reason: R8: Adasum still converges at global batch 1024, supporting V5's qualification that adapting the training recipe can avoid the penalty within the same epoch budget.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports that training with Adasum, which adaptively combines gradients across workers, converged at the large batch within two epochs. This result remains unverified.

relationships.condition: MNIST LeNet-5 with Sum at global batch 1024, separately tuned learning rate, two epochs
relationships.reason: R10: tuned Sum remains substantially below the convergent Adasum run despite learning-rate tuning, showing a residual large-batch penalty under the aggressive fixed budget.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports substantially lower performance with tuned Sum, which adds gradients across workers, than with Adasum, which adaptively combines them. This comparison remains unverified and changes the gradient aggregation method.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
